messages:
Sam (Support): Hey team — customer ACME reported repeated 429s during a short traffic spike despite being on a paid plan with moderate quota. They say it happened during a 90s batch job that fires ~120 concurrent requests. Customer wants to know how burst credits and smoothing work and if we can avoid these interruptions. Attaching short repro and headers below.

Rhea (CSE): Do we know whether they’re on Hosted or Dedicated? Also need the exact plan + quota numbers.

Sam (Support): Hosted API. Plan = Pro (200 rps baseline, 10k tokens/minute). They were sending bursts: roughly 120 concurrent requests for 90s, peak token rate ~15k/min.

Jordan (SRE): Quick summary of infra: hosted endpoints enforce a token-bucket per API key with a short-term burst allowance (burst credits) and a smoothing controller that limits sustained spikes to protect multi-tenant capacity. If the burst bucket is exhausted you’ll see 429 + Retry-After. Burst credits refill slowly (minutes) unless customer is on Reserved/Dedicated where bucket size is larger.

Sam (Support): Here’s minimal repro curl loop customer sent:

```bash
for i in {1..120}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
    -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}' &
done
wait
```

Sam (Support): Example response headers from their failed requests: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 8
x-redwood-rate-limit: 200
x-redwood-rate-remaining: 0
x-redwood-rate-reset: 1718745660
x-redwood-burst-credits: 0/60
```

Rhea (CSE): That x-redwood-burst-credits header is helpful — shows bucket capacity 60 tokens, currently drained. Reasonable to explain to ACME that short-lived spikes consume credits fast.

Jordan (SRE): Actionable options: 
- Short term: recommend client-side smoothing + exponential backoff. Add random jitter to avoid simultaneous retries.
- Mid term: increase bucket by upgrading to Dedicated/Reserved or request a burst quota bump. Add a canary rollout to spread requests if possible.
- Immediate workaround: reduce concurrency to < 60 (or whatever bucket size) during dense jobs, or pace requests to ~200 rps steady-state.

Marta (Billing): If they want larger burst allowance on Hosted we can grant a temporary pilot bump but billing needs sign-off (possible upgrade or short-term overage). I can fast-track a 7-day trial bump if they accept terms. @Sam can you confirm their account email and billing contact?

Sam (Support): Confirmed: ops@acme.co is billing contact. I’ll ask them if they want the trial bump.

Rhea (CSE): Also forwarded to the onboarding guide: recommend queuing layer (e.g., SQS/Kafka) with worker concurrency to smooth traffic. Provide sample client strategy: token-bucket local limiter that refills at 200 rps and allows short bursts up to 60, plus a retry policy that respects Retry-After.

Jordan (SRE): For the engineering team: we should add a more visible signal in Console — show current burst-credits for API keys in real time and surface a "request temporary burst" button. Filing ticket to product.

deploy-bot: Deployment: rate-limiter-updates v2 rolled out to 3 regions at 2024-06-18T09:12Z :rocket:

Sam (Support): Customer asked for exact repro steps we used to verify. I documented:
1) Use their API key in the loop above.
2) Run for 90-120 concurrent curls.
3) Observe 429s and headers; capture first 20 failing responses.
4) Switch to throttled run: change loop to 40 concurrent and rerun — confirm success.

Rhea (CSE): Suggested canned response for ACME: 
"Short answer: bursts consume a finite pool of burst credits. If a short batch consumes all credits you will see 429s until the bucket refills. Options: smooth traffic, request a temporary burst bump, or upgrade to Dedicated/Reserved for higher sustained/peak allowances. We can also work with you to add a short-lived pilot burst increase while you re-architect."

Jordan (SRE): I'll attach logs (request ids redacted) to the ticket. Main metrics to include: api_key, ts, tokens_sent, concurrent_requests, x-redwood-burst-credits.

Marta (Billing): I can do a one-time pilot bump. Sam — please get written approval from ops@acme.co and CC billing.

Sam (Support): Copying suggested client-level code to smooth (node example):

```js
// simple leaky bucket client-side
const limiter = createLimiter({rate: 200, burst: 60});
await Promise.all(requests.map(r => limiter.schedule(() => fetchAPI(r))));
```

Rhea (CSE): Also suggested adding instrumentation to their job to emit per-second request counts so we can tune.

Sam (Support): ACME replied: they prefer the short pilot bump while they implement smoothing. Approved, ops@acme.co okayed 7-day bump.

Marta (Billing): Created invoice note and temporary increase. Will confirm when applied.

Jordan (SRE): Applied a temporary +100 burst credits for that API key at 2024-06-18T11:03Z — monitor for 24h and revert automatically. I’ll add a dashboard panel for this key.

Sam (Support): Closing loop with customer. They did the throttled run and no 429s. They’ll implement smoothing in prod next week. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Rhea (CSE): Filed follow-up ticket to track whether they ultimately upgrade to Dedicated. Marking as "resolved-pending" and will check back in 10 days.

Jordan (SRE): +1 — add regression alert: if >5% 429s in 5 mins for this key, page oncall.

Marta (Billing): noted in billing system.

Sam (Support): done — thread archived.
